podcast-joerogan-wRDnL61LiPc:
Former CIA officer Mike Baker talks about the secret world in episode 1617 of the Joe Rogan Experience. Baker spent years in field work for the agency before moving into private security and TV commentary. His visits mix spy craft with dry humor and straight talk.

Baker explains how intelligence work really runs, far from the movie version. He and Rogan cover hot spots, threats, and how agencies read weak signals before attacks. Rogan asks what the public gets wrong about spies and their bosses. The result is a grounded tour behind the curtain from a man who worked there.
podcast-joerogan-eKUf_nL28Pc:
Young champion Terence Crawford brings trainer Bo Mac to Rogan's MMA Show number 76. Crawford had not yet beaten Errol Spence Jr. Rogan ranks him among the best boxers alive.

Rogan praises how smoothly Crawford switches stances mid-fight. He compares that skill to Marvin Hagler at his peak. Crawford and his trainer talk craft, patience, and waiting for big fights. The episode now plays like an early chapter: a gifted fighter, still chasing full respect, explaining skills that later made him a household name for fight fans. Fans can hear the greatness Rogan already saw.

20857-spacehounds-of-ipc:
Fine scratches score the hull of a vast cruiser in Spacehounds of IPC. Each groove marks some stray body's bid for right of way in the void. E. E. Smith lingers on that scarred mass to set his scale.

Interplanetary patrol crews hunt space pirates among the planets in Smith's tale. Bold rescues, vast ships, and ray fights fill its pages at speed. Smith helped forge space opera in the pulp magazines of the 1930s. Spacehounds shows his early form: huge craft, brave crews, and a solar system wide open for war and wonder.
